question: Which decommissioned ship of the Indian Navy was announced to be converted into a submerged museum in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Guldar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **INS Guldar** is a decommissioned ship of the **Indian Navy** that is set to be converted into a submerged museum. This decision aims to preserve its historical significance and contribute to maritime tourism.
 
• The conversion of decommissioned ships into museums is a common practice to retain the legacy of the nation’s naval history while promoting awareness and education about maritime heritage.
 
• The announcement of converting **INS Guldar** into a submerged museum was made in **2025**, recognizing its historical importance and potential contribution to naval history.
 
• The initiative of converting decommissioned ships into museums reflects the nation's commitment to honoring its maritime achievements and educating citizens and tourists about naval history and defense mechanisms.
 
• This museum will serve as a means of preserving the ship’s legacy while offering visitors a unique experience to explore its history and contribution to national defense.
 
• The project aligns with similar initiatives globally, where historic naval vessels are transformed into museums to promote public engagement and preserve naval heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **INS Guldar:**

 
 
• **INS Guldar** was a prominent vessel of the Indian Navy, playing a significant role in safeguarding maritime borders during its operational years.
 
• Decommissioned after decades of service, the ship represents an integral part of India’s naval history and achievements.
 
• The initiative of transforming it into a submerged museum will help preserve its history and showcase it to the public, ensuring that its legacy is not forgotten.
 
 
 
• **Other Decommissioned Ships of the Indian Navy:**
 
 
• **INS Vikrant:** India’s first aircraft carrier, which was decommissioned in 1997 and later turned into a museum ship. It played a critical role in the **1971 Indo-Pak War**.
 
• **INS Viraat:** Another aircraft carrier decommissioned in 2017, with plans to convert it into a museum ship, although these plans have faced challenges.
 
• **INS Khukri:** A warship lost during the 1971 war, which has been memorialized as a museum in Diu.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Naval Museums:**
 
 
• Naval museums serve as an educational tool, providing insights into the nation’s maritime history, technology, and naval defense systems.
 
• Such museums also contribute to tourism and cultural preservation, attracting visitors interested in historical and military exhibits.
 
• Countries like the **United States**, **Russia**, and the **United Kingdom** have also converted decommissioned warships into museums, highlighting the global significance of such practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Submerged Museums:**

 
 
• Submerged museums are designed to provide an underwater experience, allowing visitors to explore the ship’s interiors through special equipment or guided tours.
 
• These museums highlight the architecture, design, and operational history of decommissioned vessels.
 
• They also serve as artificial reefs, contributing to marine biodiversity and promoting environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Submerged Museums:**
 
 
• **USS Arizona Memorial:** Located in Pearl Harbor, this submerged museum commemorates the lives lost during the **World War II attack**.
 
• **HMAS Sydney:** An Australian warship wreck converted into a heritage site and museum.
 
• **HMS Belfast:** A British naval ship preserved as a museum on the River Thames in London.
